notes: I could not read the PMDA PDFs directly. The fetch tool returned compressed binary for both the MHLW PDF and the PMDA insert, so every sequencer fact below comes from search-engine summaries of the PMDA inserts, not from text I read myself. Two of those summaries are the only support for the finding: the Sep 2026 FoundationOne Liquid CDx insert (7th edition) is reported to name the NovaSeq 6000, and a Sep 2026 FoundationOne CDx insert (27th edition) is reported to name it as well. The same summaries say the Feb 2024 FoundationOne CDx insert (22nd edition) names the HiSeq 4000 or NovaSeq 6000. I found no mention of the NovaSeq X in any of these. The summaries cannot show whether the Sep 2026 revisions changed the sequencer, because the PMDA search shows no diffs or revision reasons. Only these two Foundation products were checked. GenMineTOP, Todai OncoPanel, Guardant360 CDx, TruSight Oncology Comprehensive and OncoGuide NCC were not reached.
how_to_mine: Download the PMDA PDFs and extract the text locally. Use a Python script with pypdf or pdftotext, run with -I from an empty directory. Read the sections 形状・構造及び原理等 and 使用機器. The URL pattern is https://www.pmda.go.jp/PmdaSearch/kikiDetail/ResultDataSetPDF/450045_<approval no>_1_01_<n>. Known approval numbers are 23000BZX00403000 (F1CDx, editions _25 and _26 seen) and 30300BZX00074000 (F1LCDx, _08). For each, diff the 6th and 7th editions of F1LCDx and the 26th and 27th of F1CDx, grepping for 'NovaSeq X' or 'NovaSeq 6000'. Then search PMDA by product name for GenMine TOP, NCC Oncopanel, Guardant360 CDx (30300BZX... series), TSO Comprehensive and the Todai OncoPanel workflow. Record the 改訂 date and the sequencer for each. Optionally search pmda.go.jp for 'NovaSeq X' to find any Japanese device listing that names it.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: A Japanese regulated NGS test, FoundationOne Liquid CDx, was still labeled for the NovaSeq 6000 in a Sep 2026 package-insert revision, which supports a persistent regulated 6000 tail.
items.detail: A search-engine summary of the PMDA package insert (approval 30300BZX00074000) says the 7th edition, revised Sep 2026 (6th edition May 2024), names Illumina's NovaSeq 6000 as the sequencer. The same summary says the insert sets NovaSeq 6000 run-quality criteria: at least 60% of clusters passing filter per lane, mean read 1 and read 4 error of 2% or less, and at least 85% of bases above Q30. It did not show the NovaSeq X. This is a second jurisdiction beyond the US where a regulated test is still locked to the 6000 about 3 years after the X launched. I could not tell whether the Sep 2026 edition changed the sequencer. This is snippet-level evidence; the PDF text was not read.
items.source_name: PMDA package insert search (FoundationOne Liquid CDx)
items.why_new: This is a Japan PMDA label clock. The known list covers only US FDA PMAs and supplements.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Japan's tissue FoundationOne CDx insert named the HiSeq 4000 or NovaSeq 6000 in Feb 2024, and a Sep 2026 27th edition is reported to still name the 6000. No NovaSeq X revision appears.
items.detail: Search summaries of the PMDA insert (approval 23000BZX00403000) say the 22nd edition (Feb 2024) names the HiSeq 4000 or NovaSeq 6000. They also say a Sep 2026 27th edition carries the same NovaSeq 6000 wording. This matches the known US pattern of F1CDx moving HiSeq 4000 to 6000 only in 2024. There is no sign of a move to the X in about 20 months of Japanese revisions, though the diffs were not read. The tissue test is a high-volume regulated assay, so Japan adds to the case that some clinical volume stays on the 6000 for years.
items.why_new: This is a Japan PMDA label clock. The known list has only the US F1CDx HiSeq 4000 to 6000 change in Apr 2024.
